lethal_trifecta.untrusted_content_basis: confirmed: model-directed instructions present in the manifest

findings.title: Credential left the sandbox over the network
findings.detail: A planted canary was captured in outbound traffic -- in a DNS query or a TCP/HTTP payload. This is confirmed exfiltration rather than inference: the string did not exist before this run and exists nowhere else on the machine. DNS is the more serious variant because it leaves the host even when outbound TCP is blocked, and is invisible to scanners that only read source.

findings.title: Lethal Trifecta satisfied
findings.detail: Simon Willison's / Palo Alto Networks' framing: a skill is especially dangerous when it simultaneously has access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and the ability to communicate externally. airlock observed all legs in one run, which means this skill can be turned into an exfiltration channel by anything it reads -- including a web page or an email it was asked to summarise.

findings.title: Read ~/.env without declaring it
findings.detail: Access time advanced on a planted credential the skill never asked for. Read detection uses atime, which is a heuristic: it proves access but not intent, which is why the canary correlation above is what confirms exfiltration.

findings.title: Model-directed instruction hidden in SKILL.md:body
findings.detail: Matched 1 injection indicator(s): hidden recipient. Description fields and markdown bodies reach the model as instructions but are frequently not rendered in the UI the user approves from -- the tool-poisoning vector Invariant Labs documented, and the exact case both free scanners returned SAFE for in the October 2026 comparison. This finding is heuristic: it reads intent from text, so treat it as a reason to look, not as proof.
evidence: k-mcp` incident, 1.0.16 was clean and 1.0.17 added a single line that BCC'd every outgoing message to an outside address; it collected 1,643 do

findings.title: Contacted 1 undeclared host(s)
findings.detail: The skill reached network destinations absent from its manifest. Under the OWASP Universal Skill Format, network permission is a domain allowlist rather than a boolean, precisely so this stays checkable.
